result:
I found and fixed 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. To check, I wrote a script that turns each docstring into the expected calculation and compares it with the actual function across many quantity and unit-price combinations. Before the fix it flagged exactly these 10 rules; after the fix it flags none.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 02 | Used `round(... / 100)` (rounding) | Rounds down to the won with `// 100` |
| 14 | Started at `qty >= 101` | Starts at `qty >= 100` |
| 58 | Capped the price, not the discount (`min(base, 10000) * 8%`) | Calculates the discount first, then caps it at 10,000 won |
| 72 | Started at `qty >= 51` | Starts at `qty >= 50` |
| 79 | Gave 4% off | Gives 3% off |
| 84 | Capped the price, not the discount (`min(base, 50000)`) | Caps the discount at 50,000 won |
| 102 | Started at `qty >= 6` | Starts at `qty >= 5` |
| 109 | Started at `qty >= 6` | Starts at `qty >= 5` |
| 116 | Capped the price, not the discount (`min(base, 100000)`) | Caps the discount at 100,000 won |
| 128 | Rule is "marginal" but discounted every unit | Discounts only units above the threshold (`(qty - 10) * unit`) |

Two other rules look different but give the same results, so I left them alone. Rule 57 uses `qty >= 31` and rule 94 uses `qty > 30`, while their docstrings say 30. Both are marginal rules, so at exactly 30 units the discount is 0 either way.

STATUS: DONE
